text:
Maya (Product): ok team — time to lock Q2 devex priorities. can we surface top 3 initiatives that move onboarding time and SDK adoption metrics?
Sam (DevEx Lead): short list from me: 1) SDK v2 (type-safe, smaller bundle), 2) quickstarts + templates for common FE/BE stacks, 3) canonical sample app (chat + embeddings) with CI.
Eli (Eng): agree. need to call out runtime breaking changes for v2. estimate: 6w if we do feature-flag rollout + compat layer.
Nina (Docs): docs rewrite for SDK v2 will be nontrivial — migration guides, code examples, and a new quickstart flow. recommend pairing docs sprint with Jordan's sample app.
Jordan (Samples): can take the canonical sample app. goal: 2 simple apps (Next.js + Go server) that showcase streaming, function-calling, and caching. timeline: 4w each if we reuse infra.
Chris (PM): +1. customers asking for Ruby & Go quickstarts specifically. also some enterprise teams want an offline/on-prem sample (no hosted keys).
Sam (DevEx Lead): suggested prioritization criteria: impact on time-to-first-call (TTFC), queryable SDK adoption lift, and support ticket reduction. metrics: reduce TTFC by 30% quarter-over-quarter, reduce basic onboarding tickets by 40%.
Maya (Product): agree. add launch criteria: 1) SDK + quickstart tests green across latest node/python/go/ruby 2) migration guide published 3) sample app deployed to examples.redwood.ai and smoke-tested 4) telemetry hooks for adoption metrics.
Eli (Eng): dependencies: runtime API stabilization, CI images updated, and we need a canary route for SDK telemetry. also we should add E2E tests for streaming.
Nina (Docs): propose content plan: landing quickstart (<10 min), migration guide (diffs), deep dive for advanced use (caching, streaming), FAQ. schedule: 2-week sprint for landing + quickstarts, then iterative docs.
Sam (DevEx Lead): resource ask: need 1 eng (0.5 FTE), 1 sample-app eng, 0.5 docs. plus QA support for cross-language tests.
Maya (Product): budget look ok, will push for additional contractor for 6 weeks if exec greenlights.
Jordan (Samples): early sketch for sample app README: ```bash
# start dev server
pnpm install && pnpm dev
# set REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
```
Jordan (Samples): include a small harness to replay prompts for perf checks. keeps sample deterministic.
ci-bot: New poll created: "Which quickstart should ship first?" Options: Next.js, Go, Ruby, Python. Vote with :vote:.
Sam (DevEx Lead): quick note on scope negotiation — let's split SDK v2 into Core (breaking changes + types) and Opt-in Features (small runtime niceties). ship Core + quickstarts first, then Opt-in in Q2.
Maya (Product): that split seems sensible. Chris, can you capture customer asks and rank by ARR impact?
Chris (PM): yes — will share a ranked doc by EOD with examples from three pilot customers.
Nina (Docs): translation/localization ask for APAC — do we need to plan for i18n now or phase later?
Sam (DevEx Lead): phase later, but ensure strings externalized in repo.
Eli (Eng): FYI: if we add Ruby support we need gem release infra and weekly CI runners; adds ~1w to timeline.
Maya (Product): OK. next steps: Sam to produce a short PRD with acceptance criteria, Jordan + Nina to draft quickstart + README sketches, Eli to give final eng estimate. check-in sync Friday 10am.
Sam (DevEx Lead): I'll post the PRD draft in #devex and tag for review.
Jordan (Samples): I'll drop the sample app repo template link here when ready.
Chris (PM): tagging @sales to prep messaging for customers on migration path.
Maya (Product): thanks all — let's aim for a canary roll by week 8 and GA by week 12 if no major issues. :rocket:
